message.content:
{
  "summary": "You demonstrated strong architectural reasoning in Question 2 by recommending a modular monolith with concrete trade-offs. However, marks were lost across other questions due to imprecise quality attribute response measures, inverted Circuit Breaker state definitions, calculation errors in end-to-end availability, misapplication of the CAP theorem, and an incomplete consequences section in your ADR. Addressing these conceptual and quantitative gaps will help you reach the Excellent rubric band.",
  "next_steps": [
    "Ensure quality attribute response measures use objective, quantified metrics (e.g., uptime percentages or MTTR) rather than subjective phrasing like 'most of the time'.",
    "Review core resilience and distributed systems concepts, specifically the correct state machine for Circuit Breakers and how network partitions dictate trade-offs under CAP.",
    "Complete end-to-end reliability calculations by multiplying all series subsystem availabilities, and always include balanced consequences (positive and negative) in ADRs."
  ],
  "criteria": {
    "C1": "You selected and justified suitable quality attributes. To reach Excellent, ensure both response measures are objectively measurable; your availability measure ('stay up most of the time') was too vague.",
    "C2": "Excellent work. You provided a clear recommendation justified by scenario-specific trade-offs regarding team size and performance, while explicitly acknowledging the architectural downsides.",
    "C3": "To achieve Excellent, eliminate calculation slips (5.03 hours in part b) and remember to multiply the parallel payment availability back into the overall series chain for part (c).",
    "C4": "You chose a relevant pattern, but inverted the states: Closed allows normal traffic, while Open blocks calls. For Excellent, correct the state mechanism and include tuning considerations or drawbacks.",
    "C5": "You justified reasonable choices, but misapplied the CAP theorem. Distributed systems cannot forfeit partition tolerance; you must trade Availability for Consistency (CP). Correcting this precision is required for Excellent.",
    "C6": "Your ADR sections are well-structured and scenario-specific. To reach Excellent, include at least one negative consequence or trade-off (such as eventual consistency or operational overhead) alongside the positive outcomes.",
    "C7": "Your writing was clear and met word limits. To earn full marks, ensure all in-text citations (such as [2] in Question 4) have corresponding full bibliographic entries in your References section."
  }
}
